_comment: Who is reliable on what, transcribed from the Clinical Assessment
Reliability chart in the ESD Lab Scheduling Manual (updated 7/7/26,
Sanjana Oak). This file was shipped empty for exactly this moment: the
gates read it and start enforcing with no code change.
MAPPING TO THE DASHBOARD ROSTER. The manual names people by first name.
Five map to the roster with certainty:
Sanjana  -> C03 Sanjana Oak
Lauren   -> C02 Lauren Puttock
Ramiro   -> C06 Ramiro Lucas-Mariano

Makenzie -> C05 (printed 'Soto, Morgan' on the calendar;
               the manual calls the same person Makenzie)
Maggie   -> C01 Margaret Bell   (alias confirmed by the lab)
Sofia Tous (C04) does NOT appear in the manual's
reliability chart. That is recorded here as an absence, not filled in:
on this chart they hold no independent clinical reliability, which makes
them tech rather than clinician on a visit. If that is wrong it is a
transcription question for the lab, not something to infer.
Emma, Kali and Kim are in the chart but are not coordinators - the manual
describes a separate Clinician Shifts calendar for non-coordinator
clinicians. They are recorded below under 'clinicians_not_on_roster' so
the data is not lost, but they cannot be assigned until the board models
clinicians as assignable staff.
RECENCY IS NOT RECORDED. The chart states current status only; it carries
no certification or last-practised dates. 'last_reliable_on' is therefore
left null everywhere rather than invented, and the board reports recency
as unknown instead of computing a decay from a made-up date.
status values: RELIABLE | IN_TRAINING | (absent = not certified)
source: ESD Lab Scheduling Manual, Clinical Assessment Reliability chart

visit_requirements._comment: Assessments each visit needs that require clinical reliability, from the NANO and IPSA visit-schedule tables. Baseline, PIX/RIX, OIX, OPIX, Vineland and the 24m questionnaires are not on the reliability chart and so gate nobody.
